exact_missing_items: Provider/model controls must support these configuration levels: package, seam, node, overseer, and delegated-subagent — per-thread/per-run granularity alone is insufficient
Orchestrator-managed worktrees must be visible in both Orchestrator page and Source Control view; they must be separated/partitioned from user/assistant-created worktrees
Source Control worktree view must partition worktrees as: 'Orchestrator Owned' vs 'Other'; 'Orchestrator Owned' must be further subdivided by feature seam

Source Control / Worktree Handshake research findings: Source Control is the primary operational surface for worktree inventory and user actions; Orchestrator consumes worktree identity/ownership/blocked state/lineage for run/history/recovery views
Existing docs still describe ownership as run/tier/subtask worktrees which collides with the package-based lane-pool model
Recommended boundary: Orchestrator owns package lane-pool operational truth; Source Control owns repo/worktree execution and inspection operations — this is the canonical surface division
Multiple projects can run Orchestrator concurrently; data and storage must be strictly per-project with no cross-project leakage
same issue persists with more evidence: update existing concern, append sources/evidence, allow severity/attention escalation
one concern was too broad: split into child concerns with lineage links
two concerns are actually the same issue: merge into one retained concern id; close/redirect the merged-away ids explicitly
